title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 33
paragraphs: Leaving Ionia, the fleet proceeded to conquer all the places of the Hellespont on the left as one sails in, since those on the right had already been subdued by the Persians themselves, approaching them by land. The cities of the Hellespont in Europe are these: first comes the Chersonese, in which there are many cities, then Perinthus, the strongholds of the Thracian border, Selymbria, and Byzantium. The people of Byzantium, and those of Calchedon opposite, did not even wait for the coming of the Persian ships, but had left their own land first and departed, going within the Euxine; and there they settled in the city of Mesambria. So the Phoenicians, having burned these places that have been mentioned, directed their course next to Proconnesus and Artace; and when they had delivered these also to the flames, they sailed back to the Chersonese to destroy the remaining cities that they had not sacked when they had touched there before. But against Cyzicus they did not sail at all; for the men of Cyzicus, even before the time the Phoenicians sailed in, had submitted to the king of their own accord and had come to terms with Oebares son of Megabazus, the Persian governor at Dascyleium.
